A1.reasoning:
The provided evidence describes a living patient who underwent clinical evaluation, laboratory testing (D-dimer), and compression ultrasonography of the lower limb. The ultrasound ruled out deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and identified a ruptured Baker's cyst. There is no mention of the patient's death or any post-mortem examination. Since an autopsy is a post-mortem procedure and the patient is alive with imaging performed on a living subject, no autopsy was performed.

FINAL_OPTION: No autopsy done, unknown if done, or done but results unavailable

blood vessel. Thrombosis occurs when a thrombus causes blockage
in the blood vessel. This blockage can result in partial or complete
blood ﬂow obstruction either in larger vessels such as arteries or
veins, or smaller vessels collectively termed as microcirculation.

sites will be speciﬁed, as appropriate. Thromboembolism is an
umbrella term encompassing in situ thrombus and embolus, a dis-

increase with age [79]. Troponin and B-type natriuretic peptide
